findings.title: Negative offsets passed to Django queryset slicing
findings.body: OptimizedCursorPaginator slices the queryset with a negative start (`queryset[start_offset:stop]` where start_offset = cursor.offset < 0). Django raises `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported` on negative slices, so a crafted cursor such as `?cursor=0:-5:0` causes a 500. The comment claiming the ORM handles this is wrong. The cursor is user-controlled via Cursor.from_string, which accepts negative offsets.

findings.title: BasePaginator now permits negative offsets for prev cursors
findings.body: The change `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` lets a prev cursor with a negative offset reach `queryset[negative:stop]`. Before this change it was the same failure mode, but the new code is explicitly intended to allow it, so it affects every paginator subclass. The result is an AssertionError/500 for any endpoint that accepts a crafted `is_prev` cursor. The later `len(results) == offset + limit + extra` check also uses the unclamped offset.

findings.title: Undocumented opt-in flag that unlocks a less-validated paginator
findings.body: Any org member with global access, or any superuser, can pass `optimized_pagination=true` to switch to a paginator that is meant to allow negative offsets. This is an unnecessary expansion of the attack surface on the audit-log endpoint. The paginator is also not tested, and a comment about 'permissions checked at the queryset level' does not justify skipping offset validation. The trailing whitespace on lines 71 and 89 is a minor nit.

findings.title: Eviction is based on a stale span_count and the redirect limit was reduced
findings.body: span_count is only set when a zunionstore ran, so a zadd done earlier in Python can leave the count out of date. It is only recomputed with zcard when it is 0. After a merge, span_count is the size of the last union, which is correct, but the first merge's count is overwritten. The redirect loop limit was also silently cut from 10000 to 1000, which means deeper trees are no longer joined correctly. Evicting with zpopmin drops the oldest spans silently, with no metric.

findings.title: Removed max_segment_spans enforcement while the parameter remains
findings.body: The span-count check in _load_segment_data was removed, but `max_segment_spans` is still a constructor parameter and is now unused. The Lua script hardcodes 1000 instead of using the configured value. Configuration therefore has no effect.

findings.title: Hard dependency on end_timestamp_precise
findings.body: `val["end_timestamp_precise"]` raises KeyError for any span payload missing the field, which crashes the whole batch in the consumer. Using `.get` with a fallback would be safer.
